"Потрясающее приключение с уникальной механикой!"

"Lost Winds" — это настоящая жемчужина среди мобильных и консольных платформеров. С первых минут игра завораживает своей атмосферой: живописные локации, нарисованные с любовью, и чарующая музыка создают ощущение, будто ты попал в старинную сказку.

Главная особенность — управление ветром. Это не просто механика, а настоящее волшебство: ты буквально чувствуешь, как управляешь стихией, помогая главному герою преодолевать препятствия и решать головоломки. Такой подход делает геймплей свежим и увлекательным на протяжении всей игры.

Сюжет, хоть и простой, подан очень душевно. Ты сопереживаешь мальчику Току и духу ветра Энрилу, а их дружба становится сердцем истории. Игра не перегружает сложностью, но при этом заставляет подумать, а не просто бежать вперёд.

"Lost Winds" — отличный выбор для тех, кто ищет красивое, доброе и необычное приключение. Игра оставляет после себя тёплое послевкусие и желание снова окунуться в этот удивительный мир. Однозначно рекомендую! 🌬️✨

剧情流水账：
[spoiler] 
主角Toku无意中唤醒了风精灵Enril之后一同行动。

背景故事：
Balasar的精灵滥用力量试图统治Mistralis而被封印，但现在Balasar的力量变强了，因此有很多事要干。

精灵能使用狂风让主角短暂飞起来。
边上的神庙能解锁多次狂风，让主角飞的更高更远。

从村子右边的探险家Notea那得知气流神庙就在枯干瀑布西边，神庙里有能解锁风精灵力量的东东。
得知主角打算前往那里还贴心送主角地图。

前往气流神庙解锁滑流的力量，可以用风画一条平滑的曲线。
能造曲线风，让直升机草带着主角飞到特定位置。
能引火烧藤曼，火烧植物后留下种子将植物移植到其他位置。

回冒险家的位置的村民那得知冒险家发现东边又有新神庙去了那里了。
前往村子东边底部石门，点燃火把开门，再洞穴深处发现Deo的雕像，点燃火把获得宝箱，冒险家要在这里继续探索，主角则回去询问Deo真相。

从Deo那得知他们当心Balasar解除封印带来的威胁，为此他转移了力量到秘密地点并除了Deo之外没人知道。
甚至连Deo的记忆也被封印在4个箱里里，之前主角解除了第一个箱子的封印，还有3个，最近的箱子在西边的洞穴里。

前往西边的神庙获取漩涡的力量。
旋风能造旋风让物品悬空，之后使用狂风能砸碎物品。
使用边上会发声的圆球悬空旋转让声波击碎水晶开门。

继续探索使用风车草通过高处的出口到达箱子区域开箱子。

开完箱子回去找Deo，得知最后2个箱子的位置。
西边最高峰和东边遗落村子内，并送主角斗篷，装备斗篷后主角可以随着滑流移动！（自带风车草）

有了斗篷后2个位置的箱子获取就很方便了。

打开箱子后回去找Deo得知他已经想起了一切记忆。
他把力量交给了村子的守护神巨大的石头怪Magmok那，石头怪就在第一个箱子底层。
当Deo满心欢喜放出对方后发现对方被黑暗污染了，变Boss了，开始Boss战。

勉强打过初代Boss，丢火烧手部和头部的怪物生成点，烧完了主角上去拔出，中间再用石头砸怪物头部，最后黑头怪物变绿头Magmok后将力量归还给Deo。

邪恶的Balasar脱离Magmok，Deo力量恢复。
在Magmok的帮助下村子恢复往日辉煌。
Deo使用力量将信息带到Mistralis的其他隐藏精灵那。
他呼唤其他精灵帮助Enril从灵石中释放出来。
不过听到呼唤的不仅仅有精灵，黑暗深处的怪物也听到了小男孩和Enril的故事···

Though I had enjoyed my time playing this there were a few downs.

Some of the major downsides for me was the spinning mechanic and the interactions with the splorp spawner. 
-The spinning just didn't feel instinctive and the instructions were unclear to me. So much so I had to look up gameplay to really get a good grasp of it. This was especially bad for me as it's something I had to learn in order to progress with the game and it wasn't a mechanic I liked using
-For the splorp spawner, walking up to it is not intuitive at all. Would loved to have had a tutorial of sorts to show how to deal with them as later it is essential for the end. Again had to look up a gameplay as this is another progression stopper.  
-There also was a few other things like there where parts where I was soft-locked so I had to reset from the last save point and the non re-activeness of the boss really stumped me as it was like I was doing nothing to the boss.

All that being said, the ups for sure outweighs the downs.
-I absolutely loved the music, so cozy and suitable for the asthetic of the game. I also liked the enemy music queues. Though a little jarring and sudden sometimes, they were very helpful.
-It was amazing how both the environment and the npcs react to the wind.
-I really liked how there were no massive consequences for platforming mistakes like fall damage or outright death. It let me just enjoy the game.
-The savepoints were very forgiving too.

[code]Esse é um daqueles jogos que te conquistam não pela grandiosidade, mas pela simplicidade encantadora e um toque de magia no ar. No papel de Toku, um garotinho que parece tão comum à primeira vista, somos logo apresentados ao poder de Enril, o espírito do vento. E é aí que a aventura se torna algo muito especial, porque a sua conexão com o jogo vai além de apenas controlar um personagem—você literalmente se torna o vento![/code]
[list]

[*]A mecânica é a alma de LostWinds. Ao invés de apenas correr e pular como em outros jogos de plataforma, aqui você desenha o caminho do vento para carregar Toku pelas áreas, lançar inimigos para longe ou resolver quebra-cabeças delicadamente intrincados. Não é só sobre precisão, mas sobre fluidez e ritmo, como se você estivesse dançando com o vento. É intuitivo e extremamente satisfatório, uma verdadeira obra-prima de como os controles podem se integrar perfeitamente à experiência.

[*]E os visuais? São um deleite para os olhos! Com um estilo artístico que mistura aquarela e tons suaves, cada cenário transmite uma sensação de serenidade. É como passear por uma pintura em movimento, com a trilha sonora calma e cativante guiando seus passos. A pequena aldeia, as cavernas e as montanhas possuem um charme peculiar que te faz querer explorar cada cantinho, não pela obrigação de encontrar segredos, mas pela simples alegria de se perder em sua beleza.

[*]Por baixo dessa camada de mecânicas criativas e visuais belíssimos, está uma narrativa simples, mas tocante, sobre Toku tentando salvar seu mundo do vilão Balasar. Não espere reviravoltas de tirar o fôlego, mas há uma ternura genuína na forma como a história é contada. Cada diálogo e cutscene traz um sorriso no rosto e, às vezes, uma pontinha de melancolia. É como voltar à infância, quando tudo o que importava era a sensação de aventura e descoberta.

[*]é curto, daqueles jogos que você termina em uma tarde tranquila, mas o impacto que deixa no seu coração é duradouro. Não é um épico que tenta competir com gigantes, mas uma experiência singela que se destaca por sua própria essência. Ao final da jornada, quando os créditos sobem, há uma sensação de paz, como se você tivesse sido levado por uma brisa leve em uma tarde ensolarada.
[/list]

[b]Se você gosta de jogos que entregam algo diferente e deixam o coração aquecido, dê uma chance a LostWinds. Porque, às vezes, é o vento suave que nos leva às experiências mais inesquecíveis. 🍃[/b]

I'll start off by saying I didn't know anything about this game when I got it, so, how do you know if you're the audience of this game?

I'd say this is a kind of easy game that's great for children or people who want a more casual, relaxing experience. The main reason why I say this is, the controls and mechanics are very simple and the challenges are mainly from the puzzles, not from the enemies. The controls are basically left/right and use your mouse for everything else, so it's really easy to play.

The graphics are nice, cute, colorful. The game is very much a 2D platformer and there's a little bit of a story although if you've played games before or watched cartoons and/or movies, the story is quite generic (basically the classic "our land is in peril, go on a fetch quest to defeat the enemy and save our town", type of story).

So if you like games where it's nearly impossible to die (there are lives, but I never felt any real risk to lose them) with cute characters, graphics, music and story and that you can easily finish in one afternoon or two, you'll probably like this game.

If you like more of a challenge, more sophisticated controls and mechanics, a game with risks where dying means something, with enemies and dangers everywhere and where you feel you're battling for your life, then this is likely not for you (mind you, you can like both types too... I do).

I personally feel like this game doesn't offer much when it comes to fun and excitement although that's obviously very subjective. But the controls and mechanics never go far enough where you feel like "I want to do that just for fun". Even the final boss battle felt absolutely non-threatening. There's some exploration and secret hunting but even that feels easy. 

I think the best audience for this game is children who are getting acquainted with controls, people with nostalgia for when it came out and people who want a short, cute and easy game to relax and have a good time.

Let me start by saying that this game is very prone to crashes. How often it crashes depends on who's playing it, for me it would sometimes crash a minute into starting it and other times it'd run perfectly with no crashes. There is a reliable auto-save function so it's more annoying than it is damaging, but still, proceed with caution.

If you're willing to fight through that then what you have here is a very brief and easy but relaxing and charming little vania from the Wii Shop Channel. You can move left and right normally but have to flick the mouse cursor to make your character jump or move objects around. It works for the most part and lends to some pretty clever puzzles. The world is also quite small but feels very well connected and easy to backtrack through. I also find the visual style very charming, though opinions may vary on the blocky Wii-era look.

For full price I think the game is a bit too short and simple to be worth the price, especially if you're one of the people who can barely get it to work. But once it goes on sale I'd certainly recommend it.
